bullets.text: Built a ROS 2 perception pipeline processing simulated camera frames at 24 FPS on a laptop CPU
Added rosbag replay and timestamp checks to reproduce camera-processing failures
Implemented an Open3D point-cloud filter and evaluated it on 120 synthetic warehouse scenes
Compared voxel filtering and statistical outlier removal using point retention and runtime
Trained a PyTorch segmentation baseline, reaching 72% validation mIoU on held-out synthetic images
Separated training and validation scenes and reported per-class confusion matrices
Built a Python validator that detects dropped frames and non-monotonic camera timestamps
Generated synthetic sensor faults and added regression cases for each failure category
Implemented OpenCV camera calibration using rendered checkerboards and known camera intrinsics
Compared recovered intrinsics against simulator ground truth and inspected reprojection residuals

cover_letter.text: I am applying for the Perception Engineer role at Example Robotics. My synthetic coursework example combines ROS 2 camera processing with PyTorch segmentation and point-cloud filtering.

I built a camera-processing pipeline and added rosbag replay and timestamp checks to reproduce failures. In related projects, I evaluated filtering on synthetic scenes and separated training and validation data for a segmentation baseline.
I would welcome a discussion about how these methods relate to your perception stack. My available evidence covers simulated inputs; deployment on production robots would require further validation.
